name: Missouri Tallgrass Prairie
blurb: Bluestem, prairie-chickens and the fire that keeps the grassland open.

tip.title: Take away fire
tip.text: Fire clears dead growth and stops trees taking over. Set Fire to -100% and watch the grasses, then the animals that depend on them.

sources.title: Missouri Dept. of Conservation field guide: big bluestem

notes: Feeding links were checked against the sources listed where they state them. Where the sources are silent, links come from general ecological knowledge and are illustrative. The sources are thin on predator and prey details for the prairie, so the links for predators lean most on general knowledge. Feeding links that match a GloBI (Global Biotic Interactions) record are marked in the node details, with a link to the records. A few links were added from GloBI records.

nodes.desc: A tall dominant prairie grass. The MDC says prairie species such as prairie-chickens and Henslow's sparrows indirectly depend on it, and it is excellent forage for livestock.
A shorter bunchgrass of drier prairie ground.
The MDC says historically vast herds disturbed the prairie in ways that helped maintain it. Today only small managed herds remain.
Browses wildflowers and young plants. Wikipedia notes its droppings spread nutrients that support plant diversity.
Chew grasses and wildflowers all summer and feed birds, badgers and many other predators.
Eats grasses and wildflowers and is prey for hawks, coyotes and bobcats.
A small grass-eating rodent and a staple for hawks, harriers, coyotes and badgers.
Eats seeds and insects, hibernates, and is a main prey of badgers and hawks.
Hunts voles, ground squirrels, rabbits and birds from perches over open ground.
Digs out ground squirrels, pocket gophers and other rodents. Wikipedia lists snakes, ground-nesting birds and insects as other prey.
Ambushes rabbits, rodents, birds and young deer along woodland edges.
Today's top predator of the prairie. Eats rabbits, rodents, birds and fawns.
Warm-season grasses grow fastest in summer heat.
Rain falls mostly in spring and early summer and sets how tall the grass grows.
Fire clears dead growth and keeps trees from taking over. Wikipedia and the MDC both describe prairies as fire-adapted.

nodes.name: Fungi, earthworms & bacteria
nodes.desc: Break down dead grass and dung and return nutrients to the soil.

story: Missouri Tallgrass Prairie is located in Missouri, USA, at coordinates 37.5, -94.6. This grassland supports species such as bluestem, bison, deer, and the greater prairie-chicken.
matters: The tallgrass prairie ecosystem is home to diverse species like milkweed, voles, and badgers. Very little of the original tallgrass prairie remains across North America.
